column3: The reduce-motion blocks of ingle-motion.css restate the selectors they reset at matching or higher specificity: .im-swap > :not([data-active]), .im-swap-icon > :not([data-active]), .im-tab[data-closing], .im-lift[data-settling], and the press rules as .im-press:active:not(:disabled, [aria-disabled="true"]) and .im-send:active:not(:disabled); the same text sits in the OS media query and :root[data-motion="reduce"]
column4: Under the OS rule the bare resets (.im-swap > *, .im-tab, .im-lift at (0,1,0); .im-press:active, .im-send:active at (0,2,0)) lost to the (0,2,0) and (0,3,0) rules they were meant to undo, so swaps blurred and scaled, closing tabs shrank, a dropped tab slid, and buttons still pressed in; the in-app setting worked only because its :root prefix raises specificity. Fixed at the source, and the drive handoff copy matches byte for byte
column5: Chromium computed styles with reducedMotion reduce, before -> after: inactive icon swap scale(.6) blur(2px) -> none; text swap translateY(4px) blur(2px) -> none; closing tab scale(.96) over 140 ms -> no transform, opacity only over --dur-reduce (120 ms); settling lift translate/transform/box-shadow 200/140/140 ms -> no transition; .im-press and .im-send while held scale(.97) -> none. With :root[data-motion="reduce"] the closing tab (real classes im-tab im-lift im-flip) used to vanish instantly, because :root[data-motion="reduce"] .im-flip { transition: none } at (0,3,0) beat .im-tab[data-closing]'s durations; it now fades over 120 ms like the OS path. The rest show no transform or transition in-app, before and after
